neighbours.label: tokens of a stock contrast pair of stereotyped roles ('the good cop and the bad cop', 'the nice guy and the villain'); the same nouns outside a stock pairing stay low
fire: In every interview they played the good cop and the bad cop with suspects.
Our parents split the roles: Dad was the nice cop and Mom was the strict cop.
The film gives us the usual hero and the usual villain in matching hats.
At the negotiation, one lawyer was the friendly cop and the other the mean cop.
Every sitcom family has the sensible sister and the wild sister.
In the old westerns there was always the good guy and the bad guy.
The two managers took turns being the gentle cop and the harsh cop.
Detectives often act out the soft cop and the tough cop routine.
quiet: In every interview they asked suspects the same questions twice.
Our parents split the chores: Dad cooked and Mom cleaned the kitchen.
The film gives us two brothers in matching hats on a long journey.
At the negotiation, one lawyer read the contract and the other took notes.
Every sitcom family has a kitchen and a living room set.
In the old westerns there was always a long ride across the desert.
The two managers took turns opening the shop in the morning.
Detectives often review the evidence late at night.

notes: Card: top peak ' and' in 'the nice cop and the nasty cop'; most others are ' a' in similes ('as solid as a', 'sober as a judge').
